title: How will Manchester Pride be different this year?

input.lead: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
input.summary: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
input.evidence_text: The August bank holiday weekend has been home to Manchester Pride for more than 40 years From its humble beginnings in 1985 as a fundraiser for Monsall Hospital's HIV and Aids ward, Manchester Pride grew into one of the country's biggest LGBTQ+ events When the company behind it went into voluntary liquidation last year, many were worried there would be no Pride in 2026 But Manchester City Council tried to allay fears when, in January, it announced that a new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC), Manchester Village Pride, would take over the running of the four-day event Manchester Village Pride is run by volunteer directors and is mainly made up of businesses from Manchester's Gay Village Venues in the area have loaned the new organisation £120,000 to support the planning and delivery of the event

title: Manchester Airport warns passengers ahead of busy bank holiday

input.lead: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday
input.summary: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday
input.evidence_text: Passengers travelling through Manchester Airport over the August bank holiday weekend have been warned to check how they pack to help reduce delays during one of the busiest weekends in the airport's history The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has urged travellers to avoid packing battery-powered devices in hold luggage as they pose a fire risk It said bags may have to be offloaded if items such as vapes and power banks are found in them About two million passengers are expected to depart from airports across Great Britain during the weekend, according to the regulator Anthony Shaw, a security team leader in the airport's hold baggage screening team, said staff often find devices including vapes, power banks and tablets in checked luggage "If the battery gets too hot, or is faulty, it can catch fire without warning," he said

title: Bolton Food and Drink Festival to attract 500,000 visitors

input.lead: Top chefs, live bands and free samples are promised for the four day event
input.summary: Top chefs, live bands and free samples are promised for the four day event
input.evidence_text: More than half a million people are expected to attend Bolton's Food and Drink Festival as over 100 food vendors will serve up tasty meals and drinks over four days Big name chefs include James Martin, Marco Pierre White and Nisha Katona will serve up cooking demos The festival site is spread across the town centre and organisers suggest Victoria Square information point is the best place for visitors to collect a free guide to help plan their day Debbie Newall, Bolton Council's executive cabinet member for culture, said: "This is an opportunity to support local traders, celebrate fantastic food and drink, and showcase the very best of Bolton." "From artisan stalls and celebrity chef demonstrations, to live music and family activities, there is something for everyone to enjoy "We are so proud of the continued success of the festival, and I urge everyone to visit and show their support."

title: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans

input.lead: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
input.summary: Salford City Council sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043
input.evidence_text: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans - BBC News Image caption, Mike McCusker is the council's lead member for planning By Richard Stead North West Published 1 hour ago Members of the public are being invited to have their say about plans to build nearly 35,000 new homes in Salford over the next 17 years - while also protecting the city's greenery. Extending the council's home-building plans by four years, a new document has sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043. Deputy mayor and planning boss Mike McCusker said: "We will have a brand new development plan, which will give us a good pipeline of new homes as well as protection from developers, who could successfully appeal against planning applications which the council has rejected. "At the same time its important to protect our valuable green spaces for local people." Salford Council's existing local plan, which is part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places For Everyone strategy, outlines sites to be developed until 2039. Image caption, The draft local plan outlines the ambition to build warehouses on empty land next to the Salford Community Stadium The city has been one of the fastest growing in the UK over recent years, with its population rising to 294,000 in 2024 - an increase of 34% since 2001. Most of that growth has been in the city centre - and at Salford Quays - but there have also been new homes built on former green belt land in areas like Boothstown. Councillors will vote on the draft local plan before the end of this year and it will then be submitted to the government for final approval. title: Hackers steal data from millions of UK airport customers

input.lead: About 8.7 million customers had their data accessed and a ransom was demanded
input.summary: About 8.7 million customers had their data accessed and a ransom was demanded
input.evidence_text: Hackers steal data from millions of UK airport customers - BBC News Image source, EPA Image caption, About 8.7 million customers across three UK airports had their data accessed By Georgie Docker and Mat Trewern , North West Published 27 August 2026 Three major UK airports have been hit by a "cyber security incident" in which criminal hackers accessed the data of almost nine million people and demanded a ransom. Manchester Airports Group (MAG), which owns Manchester, East Midlands and London Stansted airports, said customers' contact details, vehicle registrations and postcodes were obtained by hackers at the weekend. MAG told the BBC the hackers demanded a ransom fee for the return of the data, which the group said it refused to pay. The sum of the ransom fee was not disclosed. The firm said "at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised" and the system hacked did not hold customers' bank or payment details. The data of about 8.7 million customers was accessed. The majority of the data accessed was restricted to customer email addresses and related to WiFi sign-ups within the airports' terminals, MAG said. MAG said in a statement: "We would like to reassure customers that Manchester Airport Group takes the security of customer information extremely seriously and we apologise for any inconvenience or concern caused." Image caption, East Midlands Airport was one of those affected, along with Manchester and London Stansted The firm said it only became aware of the hack on Tuesday and quickly prevented the hackers gaining any more access, and notified affected customers. title: MND patient in race to access life-extending drug Tofersen

input.lead: Marc Powell has rare form of MND and has been waiting months for drug that could slow the effects
input.summary: Marc Powell has rare form of MND and has been waiting months for drug that could slow the effects
input.evidence_text: North West health correspondent Published 27 August 2026 A man with a rare form of Motor Neurone Disease (MND) says he could die within a year while waiting for access to a treatment that could significantly prolong his life Marc Powell, from Whaley Bridge, Derbyshire, has the SOD1 variant of the disease, which affects fewer than 100 people in the UK Drug manufacturer Biogen is supplying Tofersen free of charge to specialist centres, including Salford Royal, while the NHS decides whether to fund it However, hospitals must cover the costs of administering it, so numbers are limited. The Northern Care Alliance NHS Trust said Tofersen was not currently commissioned by NHS England and required specialist expertise and support to deliver safely Marc, who celebrated his 60th birthday this week, was diagnosed with MND in January after noticing problems with his speech "I got home and sobbed my heart out with my wife," he said

title: Speed limits and lane closures for M6 viaduct upgrade works

input.lead: Work will begin on replacing the M6 Thelwall Viaduct's joints on 1 September
input.summary: Work will begin on replacing the M6 Thelwall Viaduct's joints on 1 September
input.evidence_text: Speed limits and lane closures for M6 viaduct upgrade works - BBC News Image source, Anthony O'Neill/Geograph Image caption, The viaduct's joints have "reached the end of their operational lifespan", National Highways says By Georgie Docker North West Published 27 August 2026 Speed limits and lane closures are being imposed on a motorway viaduct as work is carried out to replace its bridge joints. The £27m "essential" upgrade will begin on the Thelwall Viaduct on the M6 in Lymm, Warrington, on 1 September. A full time contraflow system will be introduced from 12 October, as well as a temporary 40 mph (64 kmh) speed limit and narrow lanes. National Highways said the viaduct, which crosses the Manchester Ship Canal and the River Mersey, was "built several decades ago" and the work was needed for safety reasons. Work will be done on one carriage way at a time. Image source, Peter McDermott/Geograph Image caption, Work will be carried out overnight All lanes - northbound and southbound - will stay open during the day, with one lane open overnight on the carriageway being worked on. "Our road network is ageing, and many key structures, including Thelwall Viaduct, were built several decades ago," Chris Court from National Highways said. "The viaduct's joints have now reached the end of their operational lifespan, making replacement essential to maintain safety and reliability for road users." The project is due to be completed by the beginning of 2028. title: Swinton Park Golf Club: 700 homes proposed for former course

input.lead: Residents are being asked for views on a scheme including public open space and sports facilities
input.summary: Residents are being asked for views on a scheme including public open space and sports facilities
input.evidence_text: Swinton Park Golf Club: 700 homes proposed for former course - BBC News Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, The former Swinton Park Golf Club site has been closed since September 2020 By Charlotte Hall , Local Democracy Reporting Service and Haider Saleem , Reporting from North West Published 27 August 2026 Proposals for about 700 homes on a former golf course have raised residents‘ concerns about traffic and pressure on local services. Wain Estates is consulting on the future of the 100-acre former Swinton Park Golf Club site in Swinton, Greater Manchester, which closed in September 2020. The developer said more than half the site could become public open space, with affordable homes, sports facilities and housing for older people also proposed. But Mike Hartney, 65, who has lived in the area for 34 years, said traffic was already "awful" and local services were oversubscribed. "Everywhere is oversubscribed already," he said. "It'll only get worse." Wain Estates said it intended to seek outline planning permission later in 2026 and the number of homes could change following technical work, public feedback and discussions with council planners. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Mike Hartney said traffic and local services were already under pressure Dave Marsh, who was a member of the golf club for more than 30 years, said the course should be restored. Mr Marsh, who campaigns with Save Swinton Park Golf Club, said the grounds had remained closed throughout the coronavirus pandemic, despite appeals from the community. "It never should have closed as a golf club," he said. "We will fight it until our last breath to stop them." However, not all residents opposed developing the land. Image source, Local Democracy Repo

title: Burst pipe floods Scarisbrick restaurant for second time in three years

input.lead: United Utilities apologises after a Scarisbrick restaurant, which was flooded in 2023, is deluged again
input.summary: United Utilities apologises after a Scarisbrick restaurant, which was flooded in 2023, is deluged again
input.evidence_text: A restaurant owner has said he got "deja vu" when he was told one of his venues had been flooded after a water pipe burst for the second time in three years Salique Meah, 38, was alerted by one of his employees at Nellie Restaurant and Bar in Scarisbrick, Lancashire, at about 03:00 BST on Tuesday He said the venue was previously flooded on 26 June 2023 but this time the damage was worse, with the water up to 3ft (0.9m) in places, and there was not a single thing that he could salvage Water firm United Utilities apologised to the owners of three properties who had been affected by the flooding - which was caused by a burst water main- and said it was supporting them Meah, from Oldham, said there was "lots of water everywhere in the building" and it would cost "a lot" in terms of lost business He said he had to close the restaurant for 10 months last time this happened

title: Fans share memories of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston

input.lead: Hundreds of fans went to Robin Park Arena to sign a book of condolence for the Wigan Warriors star
input.summary: Hundreds of fans went to Robin Park Arena to sign a book of condolence for the Wigan Warriors star
input.evidence_text: Fans have shared memories of the much-loved rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston and signed a book of condolence at his former club Wigan Warriors Rugby league's first knight died earlier this week aged 92 surrounded by his closest family, the club said As well as his achievements on the pitch - including scoring 571 tries in his career - a total surpassed only by Australian legend Brian Bevan in top-class rugby league - Boston has a legion of fans heartbroken at the legend's death The club's kitman, and a lifelong fan who first saw him as a child, and decades later worked for him in his pub when he retired, were among hundreds who went to Robin Park Arena to pay tribute to the star Josie Andrews held back the tears as she told BBC North West Tonight : "I fell in love with Billy Boston when I was eight "My dad took me to watch him and that is when I fell in love with Wigan rugby."

input.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
